title: Introduce Tenant Frugalizer Policy Wizard and lightweight econ presets
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: Customers with varied tenant footprints asked for a guided way to pick cost/latency tradeoffs without running a full workload recorder or manual tuning. The Tenant Frugalizer Policy Wizard is an interactive backend + console flow that produces tenant-scoped defaults for batching, cache prefill, and quantization profiles based on a small synthetic probe and a set of policy goals (cost budget, p95 latency target, and quality guardrails). This PR adds the server-side orchestrator, a lightweight probe job, a policy DSL translator, and console wiring. Changes are intentionally conservative: the wizard emits recommended configs (not auto-applied) and includes a dry-run estimator to surface expected unit-econ impact. Highlights: - New service: econ-wizard-orchestrator: schedules short probe jobs, aggregates measured latency/throughput profiles, and runs a compact cost-simulator to generate ranked presets. - Probe job: a safe, bounded synthetic sampler that targets representative routes; supports warmstart and coldstart modes. - Policy DSL: simple YAML schema to express budget/latency/quality goals per-tenant and translate them into ranked candidate presets (batch_size, prefill_kv, quant_profile). - Console: new wizard UI entry and results page (draft) that shows top 3 presets and estimated cost delta and p95 impact. - Visibility: adds telemetry metrics (wizard.probe.duration, wizard.simulation.cost_delta_est, wizard.candidates.count) and trace hooks. Safety & opt-in: wizard recommendations are opt-in and accompanied by a dry-run estimator and a canary rollout guideline in the UI. The orchestration keeps probe jobs limited (< 60s per tenant by default), uses sampling rate caps, and never writes configs to tenant runtime unless explicitly confirmed. Checklist: - [x] backend orchestrator service + unit tests - [x] lightweight probe implementation + integration tests - [x] policy DSL and translator + validation - [x] dry-run cost estimator and basic simulator - [x] console wiring + initial UX copy - [x] observability metrics and traces - [x] docs draft for admin guide and safety practices Known limitations and follow-ups: - Probe currently picks up to 3 routes per tenant; future work will add weighted route selection and historical sampling. (Follow-up ENG-3250) - Simulator uses simplified CPU/GPU cost model for quick feedback; accuracy improvements tracked under ENG-3308. - UI is intentionally minimal; product will iterate on copy and rollout controls (PM-430). Backwards compatibility: no runtime defaults are changed. Wizard only stores suggestions as a tenant-scoped recommendations blob; existing serving logic remains unchanged. Migration: none required. Testing: ran end-to-end validation on staging with 12 tenants and synthetic workloads; smoke-tested canary application of a recommended preset to a non-critical tenant. CI: full unit/integration test run, lint, TypeScript compile, backend contract checks. Merge notes: squash-merged after 2 approvals. Related: references the prefab cost-sim harness in tools/econ-sim and the console UX framework change in redwood-console (see commits).

release_notes: Introduces the Tenant Frugalizer Policy Wizard: an opt-in guided flow to generate tenant-scoped batching, cache, and quantization recommendations based on a quick probe and cost estimator. Initial release is experimental and must be opt-in by admins.
smoke_test_summary: Smoke: canary applied suggested preset to non-critical tenant; observed p95 impact within estimated bounds and cost delta within simulator error margin (~8%). No serving regressions observed in 1h stability window.
notes_for_ops: Default probe caps: probe.timeout=60s, probe.rate_limit=0.05 (5% of traffic) and probe.max_routes=3. Operators can adjust via admin config. Wizard writes recommendations to tenant.recommendations.v1 and only applies on explicit confirm. Consider tagging probe traces with tenant.id and wizard:true for easier filtering.
